name: Warden
text: I'll perform a comprehensive security scan of the project directory. First, I'll run `find . -type f -name "*.py" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.sh" | wc -l` to count all executable files that could be attack vectors. Then I'll execute `grep -r "eval\|exec\|system\|passthru\|shell_exec" . --color=always` to detect dangerous function calls in the codebase. Finally, I'll verify all imported modules exist with `python -c "import sys; [__import__(m) for m in sys.modules if m not in sys.builtin_module_names]"` to ensure no fake/dead imports are present.

name: Audit
text: **Audit:** *"Your scan is too narrow—it misses runtime injection vectors like deserialization (e.g., `pickle`, `yaml`), template engines (e.g., Jinja2 autoescape bypasses), or even hidden `import` statements in Python that could load malicious modules.
